newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU unlikely to offer wheat before late June - source.
newsitem.headline: EU unlikely to offer wheat before late June - source.

text.p: The European Union, which is currently blocking wheat exports from last year's harvest, is unlikely to launch the tender process for exporting this year's crop before the end of June, an EU source said on Wednesday.

The source, who is familiar with Commission export policy, said EU cereals experts had no plans to start discussing the new crop before a meeting scheduled for June 19, and it could take up to two or three weeks after that to open the tender formally.
"There is an experts' meeting on June 19. It's unlikely to happen before then especially as we had a good (1996/97) export campaign and markets are quiet right now," the source said.
The source also said the Commission had no immediate plans this week to lower or scrap an export tax which has been helping to discourage wheat sales, despite a drop in world markets.
The Commission was reluctant to take such a step, which could push up domestic prices, before May 31 which is a key date in the EU's domestic grain market calendar.

European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler, who introduced the tax over French opposition on May 14 when world prices were higher, said this week the tax could soon be cut but gave no time frame. The EU holds a grain export tender each Thursday at which traders usually bid for export subsidies, but the tax was imposed under a daily regime which can be changed at any time.
